name: Bronze sculpture
material: copper-alloy casting, often hollow for larger works; surface may be chased, joined, polished, patinated, gilded or inlaid
fabrication_process: create mold and wax model for lost-wax workflow
establish core and casting channels for hollow work
apply or develop patina as appropriate
visible_production_marks: casting seams or repaired joins may be subtly visible
thin edges remain metallic, not stone-like
edge_behavior: Cast edges can be crisp but transition through modeled volumes; thin projections require casting/support logic rather than carved-stone mass.
mark_making: casting seams or repaired joins may be subtly visible
thin edges remain metallic, not stone-like
color_behavior: Metallic base color varies with alloy and patina; highlights are specular and directional, not uniform orange “bronze paint.”
surface_behavior: Metal reflects environment; aged patina may be brown/black/green in varied layers, with rubbed high points and localized corrosion.
composition_behavior: Use hollow-cast object logic, stable center of mass, deliberate base or bust support, and joined-element plausibility.
structural_limitations: large thin unsupported metal sheets need structural logic
aging_weathering: fresh: warm metallic surface with finishing variation
aged: layered oxidation/patina, rubbed edges, localized corrosion
excavated: mineral accretions may be uneven

prompt_fragments.core: Render a cast copper-alloy object with true metallic reflection, chased surface detail, plausible joins and state-specific patina; model hair/cloth as cast masses, not living strands.
prompt_fragments.portrait: For a bust, use intentional shoulder/chest termination and a stable mount; let fine chasing define hair and pupils rather than photoreal pores.

evaluation_criteria: metal response changes with light/view angle
patina is layered/local rather than flat color
represented subject is fully translated into metal

sources.supports: technical examination and fabrication features of bronze sculpture

scope_note: This module controls material/production behavior. It does not select an era by itself.
